'''Daniel Gafford''' (born October 1, 1998) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Dallas Mavericks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas Razorbacks]] and was drafted in the second round of the [[2019 NBA draft]] by the [[Chicago Bulls]]. He plays both the [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] and [[Center (basketball)|center]] positions.

==High school career==
Gafford was a four star recruit in high school, and received offers in 2015 from multiple schools, including [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]], and [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]]. Gafford also used to play [[American football|football]] growing up and played at wide receiver until ninth grade at [[El Dorado High School (Arkansas)|El Dorado High School]]. He was also in the marching band and credits that to the development of his skill set.<ref>{{cite news |title=High-flying Daniel Gafford a force for surging Arkansas |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2017/12/22/high-flying-daniel-gafford-a-force-for-surging-arkansas/108858280/ |access-date=February 1, 2025 |work=[[USA Today]] |date=December 22, 2017 |archive-date=February 14, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220214061051/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2017/12/22/high-flying-daniel-gafford-a-force-for-surging-arkansas/108858280/ |url-status=bot: unknown }}</ref>

On August 1, 2015, Gafford committed to the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|University of Arkansas]].<ref>{{cite web |author=Harper, Doc |date=August 1, 2015 |title=Arkansas Basketball Recruiting: Daniel Gafford Commits to the Razorbacks |url=https://www.arkansasfight.com/2015/8/1/9085589/arkansas-basketball-recruiting-daniel-gafford-commits-razorbacks |access-date=June 21, 2018 |work=Arkansas Fight}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:Daniel Gafford.jpg|thumb|left|Gafford [[slam dunk|dunking]] for the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arizona Razorbacks]] ]]
In his first start for the Razorbacks, Gafford finished a perfect 8 for 8 shooting, along with 7 rebounds and 6 blocks against [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Gafford shines in first start|author=Hutchinson, Andrew|website=247Sports|url=https://247sports.com/college/arkansas/Article/Daniel-Gafford-shines-in-first-start-Arkansas-Razorbacks-beat-Minnesota-Golden-Gophers-95-79-112058150/|date=December 9, 2017|access-date=June 21, 2018}}</ref> Gafford posted 21 points, 10 rebounds and seven blocks against No. 14 [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Stone |first1=Chris |title=NBA Draft watch: Arkansas' Daniel Gafford has potential to thrive as traditional big man |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/nba/news/daniel-gafford-arkansas-nba-draft-2018-mock-highlights-stats-scouting-report-wingspan/4cya8wpo3onq110lpforvc19c |access-date=June 22, 2018 |work=[[Sporting News]] |date=March 2, 2018 |archive-date=February 14, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220214060127/https://www.sportingnews.com/nba/news/daniel-gafford-arkansas-nba-draft-2018-mock-highlights-stats-scouting-report-wingspan/4cya8wpo3onq110lpforvc19c |url-status=dead }}</ref> After a freshman season where he averaged 11.8 points 6.2 rebounds per game, Gafford announced that he would return to Arkansas for his sophomore year rather than declare for the [[2018 NBA draft]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Daniel Gafford to return to Arkansas rather than head to NBA|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22923623/daniel-gafford-return-sophomore-season-arkansas|date=March 26, 2018|access-date=June 21, 2018|work=espn}}</ref> After his freshman season, Gafford was named to the SEC All-Freshman team.<ref>{{cite web|title=3 Hogs honored by SEC coaches|author=Hutchinson, Andrew|url=https://247sports.com/college/arkansas/article/3-arkansas-razorbacks-honored-named-to-coaches-all-sec-teams-jaylen-barford-daryl-macon-daniel-gafford-115898207/|date=March 6, 2018|work=247 Sports|access-date=June 21, 2018}}</ref>

Gafford improved his statistics during his second year at Arkansas, averaging 16.9 points, 8.6 rebounds, and 1.9 blocks per game. He was named to the 2019 SEC All-Defensive Team, as well as a 1st Team All-SEC pick.<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.secsports.com/article/26238088/2019-sec-men-basketball-awards-announced |title=2019 SEC Men's Basketball Awards announced |publisher=Southeaster Conference |date=March 12, 2019 |accessdate=March 12, 2019}}</ref> On March 18, 2019, after Gafford's sophomore season, it was announced that Gafford would skip the [[2019 National Invitation Tournament]] to prepare for the [[2019 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web |author=Boone, Kyle |date=March 18, 2019 |title=Arkansas star Daniel Gafford, projected first-round pick, skipping NIT to prepare for NBA Draft |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/arkansas-star-daniel-gafford-projected-first-round-pick-skipping-nit-to-prepare-for-nba-draft/ |access-date=March 18, 2019 |work=[[CBS Sports]]}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Chicago Bulls (2019–2021)===
Gafford was the 38th overall selection by the [[Chicago Bulls]] in the [[2019 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|first1=Sam|last1=Smith|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/john-paxson-pleased-bulls-draft-night-additions|title=John Paxson Pleased With Bulls' Draft Night Additions|date=June 21, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=June 21, 2019}}</ref> On July 8, 2019, the [[Chicago Bulls]] declared that they had signed Gafford.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/bulls-sign-daniel-gafford|title=Bulls Sign Daniel Gafford|date=July 8, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 8, 2019}}</ref> On October 26, 2019, Gafford played his NBA debut, coming off the bench in an 84–108 loss to the [[Toronto Raptors]] with a rebound.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160673|title=Siakam, Anunoby lead Raptors over Bulls 108–84|date=October 26, 2019|website=ESPN.com|access-date=October 27, 2019}}</ref> He was assigned to the [[Windy City Bulls]] for opening night of the [[NBA G League]] season. On January 15, 2020, Gafford injured his thumb just 1 minute and 21 seconds into a match against the [[Washington Wizards]]. The next day, it was announced that he wouldn't play for around two to four weeks because he had a dislocated thumb.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Taylor |first1=Cody |title=Bulls rookie Daniel Gafford out 2–4 weeks with a dislocated thumb |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2020/01/16/daniel-gafford-dislocated-thumb-injury-timetable-nba-lineups/ |access-date=January 16, 2020 |work=Rookie Wire |date=January 16, 2020}}</ref>

===Washington Wizards (2021–2024)===
[[File:WizardsRaptors 63 (51589303743).jpg|thumb|right|Gafford [[slam dunk|dunking]] for the [[Washington Wizards]] ]]
On March 25, 2021, Gafford was traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] in a three-team trade involving the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-acquire-gafford-and-hutchison|title=Wizards acquire Gafford and Hutchison|work=NBA.com|date=March 25, 2021}}</ref> During the [[2021 NBA playoffs]], Daniel Gafford broke the record for field goal percentage (minimum 15 shot attempts) with an astounding 84.6%.

On October 18, 2021, Gafford signed a three-year, $40.2 million contract extension with the Wizards.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hughes |first1=Chase |title=Gafford gets 3-year extension with Wizards |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/washington/wizards/daniel-gafford-gets-3-year-contract-extension-wizards |access-date=October 19, 2021 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=October 19, 2021}}</ref>

On March 7, 2023, Gafford made a buzzer-beating, game-winning putback in a 119–117 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/wizards-news-daniel-gafford-has-washington-fans-hyped-with-buzzer-beater-vs-pistons|title=Daniel Gafford has Washington fans hyped with buzzer beater vs. Pistons|website=ClutchPoints|last=Villas|first=Rexwell|date=March 7, 2023|access-date=March 7, 2023}}</ref>

===Dallas Mavericks (2024–present)===
On February 8, 2024, Gafford was traded to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] for [[Richaun Holmes]] and draft compensation.<ref>{{cite web|first=Eddie|last=Sefko|title=Mavericks Acquire Washington, Gafford to Bolster Front Line|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavs-trades/|website=Mavs.com|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 8, 2024}}</ref> Two days later, on February 10, Gafford made his Mavericks debut, recording 19 points and nine rebounds in a 146–111 win over the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Doncic scores 32, Gafford shines in Dallas debut as Mavs thump Thunder 146–111|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401585376|website=ESPN.com|date=February 10, 2024|access-date=February 10, 2024}}</ref>

Shortly after joining the Mavericks, Gafford set a record of 33 consecutive made field goals, second all-time to [[Wilt Chamberlain]]'s record of 35.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 15, 2024 |title=Mavericks big man falls just short of Wilt Chamberlain's record by missing first shot in 34 attempts |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/mavericks-big-man-falls-just-short-of-wilt-chamberlains-record-by-missing-first-shot-in-34-attempts/ |access-date=March 25, 2024 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=McGregor |first=Gilbert |title=NBA most consecutive field goals made streak: Daniel Gafford comes up short of Wilt Chamberlain's all-time record |url=https://www.msn.com/ |access-date=March 25, 2024 |website=www.msn.com}}</ref> The streak lasted from March 5 to 13, 2024.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Capurso |first=Tim |date=March 15, 2024 |title=Mavericks Player Finally Misses Shot, Falls Just Short of Wilt Chamberlain Record |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2024/03/15/mavericks-daniel-gafford-misses-shot-falls-short-wilt-chamberlain-record-consecutive-made-field-goals |access-date=March 25, 2024 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |language=en-us}}</ref>

Gafford finished the 2023–2024 season as the [[List of NBA annual field goal percentage leaders|NBA field goal percentage leader]], with a percentage of 72.5% with 348 out of 480 shots made.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bhattacharya |first=Ishaan |date=April 16, 2024 |title=2023–24 NBA League Leaders: Luka Doncic Wins First Career Scoring Title |url=https://fadeawayworld.net/2023-24-nba-league-leaders-luka-doncic-first-career-scoring-title |access-date=May 1, 2024 |website=Fadeaway World |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kluska |first=Kenny |date=April 15, 2024 |title=NBA League Leaders For The 2023–24 Regular Season |url=https://lastwordonsports.com/basketball/2024/04/15/nba-league-leaders-for-the-2023-24-regular-season/ |access-date=May 1, 2024 |website=Last Word On Basketball |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Leader in NBA field goal percentage |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/C6PqIBGN8HA/ |access-date=May 1, 2024 |website=Instagram}}</ref> Gafford helped the Mavericks reach the [[2024 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] where they lost to the [[Boston Celtics]] in five games.<ref>{{cite web|title=Boston Celtics defeat Dallas Mavericks to win 2024 NBA Finals|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/boston-celtics-beat-dallas-mavericks-2024-nba-finals/|publisher=cbsnews.com|access-date=June 17, 2024|date=June 17, 2024}}</ref>

On January 15, 2025, Gafford put up a career-high 27 points, along with 12 rebounds in a 119–116 loss to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/mavericks-news-daniel-gafford-career-pelicans|title=Mavericks' Daniel Gafford sets new career-high in dominant performance vs. Pelicans|website=ClutchPoints|last=Mistretta|first=Joey|date=January 15, 2025|access-date=January 15, 2025}}</ref> On January 20, Gafford put up a career-high 31 points, along with 15 rebounds, seven blocks, three assists, and one steal in a 110–105 loss to the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/mavericks-news-dallas-jason-kidd-daniel-gafford-turnovers-hornets|title=Mavericks' honest explanation for costly mistakes in frustrating Hornets loss|website=ClutchPoints|last=Mistretta|first=Joey|date=January 20, 2025|access-date=January 21, 2025}}</ref> He signed a three-year, $54 million contract extension with Dallas on July 12.<ref>{{cite web | last=Gauruder | first=Dana | title=Daniel Gafford Signs Three-Year Extension With Mavericks | website=Hoops Rumors | date=July 12, 2025 | url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2025/07/mavericks-daniel-gafford-agree-to-three-year-extension.html | access-date=December 7, 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Gafford is an avid watcher and fan of [[anime]]. He's expressed his love and support for ''[[Black Clover]]'', stating how he named his dog after one of the characters, [[Mereoleona Vermillion]].<ref>{{cite news |title=From Melo to Ona, meet Daniel Gafford's growing family of four-legged friends|url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/mavericks/article/daniel-gafford-dallas-dogs-22184309.php |work=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |date=April 27, 2026 |access-date=May 4, 2026}}</ref> Gafford also explained how the [[manga]]'s main character, [[Asta (Black Clover)|Asta]], helped him out as a player by never giving up.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peters |first=Megan |date=January 26, 2022 |title=Black Clover Just Got a Big NBA Shoutout in This New Promo |url=https://comicbook.com/anime/news/black-clover-anime-nba-daniel-gafford/ |access-date=March 26, 2023 |website=comicbook.com}}</ref> Gafford even has anime-inspired tattoos.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cole Anthony, Daniel Gafford and Laurenz Pakter Delve Into Their Anime Origin Stories at NBA Con|url=https://www.crunchyroll.com/news/interviews/2023/7/19/nba-con-panel-interview |website=[[Crunchyroll News]] |publisher=[[Crunchyroll]] |date=July 19, 2023 |access-date=May 4, 2026}}</ref>
